subject: SLO-driven deployment runway: hosted vs reserved capacity — quick check-in
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Recap & proposed runway: latency/throughput constraints + next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — good conversation and appreciate the specificity on traffic shape. Short recap and a proposed runway so we can converge on Hosted vs Reserved (Dedicated) for the pilot:

Summary of GreenCart requirements
- Peak QPS: ~2,200 during promo windows (10–15 minute bursts)
- Steady sustained QPS: 180 qps outside peaks
- P99 tail latency target for LLM responses: < 180 ms (token streaming ok)
- Workload: short prompts + shopping-cart reranking + ~1.5k token generation budget per complex query
- Data residency: US only — no on-prem requirement for now

High-level recommendation (from the call)
- Hosted API looks attractive for quick start and dev velocity; cost-efficient for steady-state but might struggle with 10–15m burst peaks unless we use burst capacity and aggressive autoscale.
- Reserved (Dedicated) capacity gives predictable throughput and tighter latency SLOs at peak, but requires a commitment and slightly higher baseline spend.

Proposed next steps (timeline for pilot)
1) Technical pilot runbook (attached): benchmark the burst pattern against a 2-node reserved pool and an autoscale-hosted configuration. We’ll load the qps_sample_trace.ndjson you shared plus a synthetic burst pattern. (Deliverable: pilot_report.pdf)
2) Confirm SLOs and acceptable fallbacks (e.g., degrade to smaller model or cached responses during sustained overage). Please confirm whether dropping to 300 ms p99 for 2–3% of requests during extreme peaks is acceptable.
3) Pricing/commit ask: we’ll send a short pricing_estimate_v2.xlsx for the two paths (hosted burst + priority queueing vs 24/7 reserved).
4) Schedule a 60-min tech deep-dive next Tue to lock pilot infra and test windows: https://calendly.com/redwood-tech/green-cart-tech-deep-dive

Attachment references: green-cart-pilot-sla-and-benchmark-plan.pdf (pilot scope), qps_sample_trace.ndjson (your trace), pricing_estimate_v2.xlsx (estimates).

If you want us to sketch a short-run financial runway (3-month burn at projected traffic) we can add that to the estimate.

Thanks — assigning Marissa to own the pilot technical scope and Ben on pricing. I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once Alex confirms the tech-deep slot.

—

- The 2,200 qps number is measured at the edge (after our API gateway). Upstream of our service it’s about ~1,900 qps going to the LLM callers due to preliminary filtering. Happy to provide the exact raw traces.
- The 180 ms p99 is our ideal user-facing requirement; we can tolerate the 300 ms p99 for short windows but would prefer to keep it to <5% of requests during promo bursts.
- For the pilot, we prefer the least-friction path first (Hosted + reserved burst) but need to see a quantitative run vs a dedicated setup to justify a reserved commitment.

Subject: Pilot runbook + measurement plan (attached)

Alex / Priya — attaching the pilot runbook and a short measurement plan. Key engineering notes below that will influence Hosted vs Reserved behavior during bursts:

Technical notes
- Prefix/KV caching: your workload benefits from prefix caching on repeat queries; we’ll enable caching in both configs to keep comparisons apples-to-apples.
- Batching windows: hosted autoscale will batch aggressively to save cost; that reduces CPU/GPU work per token but can add a few ms to tail latency if windows grow. We’ll cap batching latency at 12 ms for the pilot.
- Cold-starts: reserved nodes avoid inference cold-starts and maintain warmed KV caches; expect ~20–40 ms lower p99 in dedicated in steady sustained traffic.
- Degradation policy proposals: (a) smaller model fallback with re-ranking, (b) token budget enforcement, (c) 429-style backpressure with graceful UX messaging.

Pilot measurement matrix (what we’ll capture)
- P50/P95/P99 generation latency (end-to-end)
- Token throughput and per-token CPU/GPU time
- Cost per 1M tokens for both configs over the test window
- Failure/overage behavior and fallback effectiveness

Action items for GreenCart
- Send raw edge traces (you mentioned you can) — we’ll hydrate the ndjson to drive the replay.
- Confirm the acceptable fallback window (2–3% at 300 ms or up to 5%?).

I attached: green-cart-pilot-sla-and-benchmark-plan.pdf and a short synthetic-driver script. Ben — I left the initial pricing estimates in pricing_estimate_v2.xlsx for reference.

—
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

- A hosted-first pilot is what we want: please run the hosted autoscale config against the trace and then a dedicated 2-node reserved run so we can see the delta.
- If the dedicated p99 advantage is >60 ms and cost delta is <40% we will likely recommend a reserved commitment to finance.

We’re locked for Tues 2028-04-10 10:00am PT for the tech deep-dive. I’ll forward the calendar invite and include the platform folks who will be on the call.
